summary.headline: TeamLease Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 6% YoY to INR3,056 crores, but EBITDA fell 31% QoQ on EdTech seasonality and appraisals.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR3,056 crores, up 6% YoY and 4% QoQ, while PBT and PAT both rose 38% YoY to INR36 crores and INR34 crores. Business EBITDA before corporate costs grew 18% YoY, but group EBITDA fell 31% QoQ as EdTech seasonality and appraisal costs hit. General staffing volume growth slowed sharply, with headcount up only 4,000 QoQ to about 2.91 lakh amid client cost pressure, GST 2.0 exits and a pause in power distribution rollouts. Management kept FY27 confidence based on mix and operating leverage, but gave no firm EBITDA guidance and said the 20% FY27 EBITDA target is uncertain. The company completed a INR238 crore buyback and agreed to exit its 30% stake in Crystal HR at full cost recovery.

financial_highlights.change: Aided by INR38 crores tax refund

financial_highlights.value: INR238 crores (8.8% of pre-buyback paid-up capital)

segments.name: General staffing
segments.commentary: Closed at about 2.91 lakh associates, up 4,000 QoQ; gross joinees about 67,600 with 28 new logos, over 2/3 under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing. Staffing EBITDA is about 1%, expected to stay flat in Q2 and improve in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Specialised staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13% YoY with headcount at 7,630 (net add of 130 QoQ, +13% YoY); 40 new logos including 15 GCCs. GCCs are 45% of associates and 67% of net revenue; margin dipped on upfront investment in Singapore and Middle East; management sees 8-9% stable EBITDA margin in 4-5 quarters.

segments.name: HR services (EdTech and RegTech)
segments.commentary: EdTech has a structurally weak Q1 and a high Q4 weight; EdTech steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 8-10%, with FY27 margin expansion going up to 8-10%. RegTech expected about 8% EBITDA margin for FY27 and now contributes meaningfully to the bottom line.

segments.name: Degree apprenticeship (DA)
segments.commentary: Net addition of about 2,100 apprentices excluding the planned exit of 5,500 headcount flagged in Q4; 18 new client logos added.

guidance_outlook: Staffing EBITDA margin flat for Q1-Q2 FY27, with margin expansion expected in Q3 and Q4 as sales and hiring investments pay off.
Management said it may or may not achieve the 20% FY27 EBITDA growth guidance, citing business and planned investments in data lake, hiring and adjacencies.
Unallocated corporate costs at the current run rate (new leadership in technology and Managing Director) to continue in future quarters.
Management expects a reasonably decent positive net addition in headcount for FY27 and a bullish outlook for the rest of the year, but gave no volume growth number.
Management expects clients to remain on path through H1 FY27, with 17,500 open positions and a healthy pipeline.
capex_capacity: Investments in sales and hiring engines planned for Q1-Q2 FY27, plus data lake spend that was not budgeted earlier.
Specialised staffing: upfront investment in Singapore and Middle East operations acquired about a year ago; margin recovery expected by Q2-Q3.
Smart meter scheme in power distribution: only about 1/4 of the INR25 crore target installed; scheme extended to March 2028 with a large awarded order book yet to be executed.
Capital allocation: buyback of INR238 crores completed (record date 3 July 2026); exit of 30% Crystal HR stake via put option at full recovery of original cost.
demand_pricing: General staffing volume growth has slowed to mid-single digit or lower; management says demand visibility has shortened from several quarters to one quarter at a time.
BFSI described as rotation rather than expansion; growth came from wallet-share gains at private banks, small finance banks and midsized NBFCs.
GST 2.0 and insurance/FMCG tax changes led some clients to move to in-house frontline models; structural client exits noted.
IT services hiring cautious and concentrated in AI and AI-adjacent skills; over 300 AI professionals deployed in the quarter; over 700 associates hired for GCC customers.
Variable markup or outcome-linked pricing used in over 65% of new logos; management says markups have been constant for many years and no near-term change is expected.
Labour codes: most clients who have implemented have preserved associate net take-home pay and absorbed the statutory cost increase; no P&L impact expected on the associate book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the general staffing volume slowdown and BFSI stress structural, and what is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Balasubramanian said demand has become harder to forecast, with visibility now a quarter at a time, and BFSI setbacks are episodic. Ramani said staffing EBITDA is about 1% and will stay flat for one to two quarters, with margin expansion from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will markups improve as the mix shifts to Tier 2-3 cities, non-BFSI accounts and variable markup contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna said there is no big near-term change; higher-margin opportunities need investment and will play out over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why are specialised staffing margins low and what is the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani attributed the dip to front-loaded investment in Singapore and Middle East operations and guided to an 8-9% stable margin in 4-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will HR services profitability improve meaningfully in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna said EdTech margin would expand to 8-10% and RegTech to about 8% on a full-year basis, with a good overall improvement in HR services EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unallocated cost increase in the segment results?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani said it reflects new leadership in technology and a new Managing Director; the current run rate will continue in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term levers to lift margin beyond 1.2-1.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani said core staffing margin will stay in its current range; the lift will come from portfolio mix, with higher-margin businesses such as specialised staffing and HR services growing faster.

risks_watch: General staffing volume growth: management says demand visibility is now one quarter at a time, with mid-single-digit or lower volume growth; watch headcount net adds and gross joinees in Q2.

Staffing EBITDA margin about 1%, guided flat in Q1-Q2 FY27 with expansion only from Q3; any slippage would put the FY27 20% EBITDA growth target further out of reach, which management said it may or may not achieve.

Unallocated corporate costs at the current run rate (new technology leadership and new Managing Director), plus unbudgeted data lake spend and planned sales and hiring investments, could keep group EBITDA growth below business EBITDA growth.
Specialised staffing margin dip from upfront Singapore and Middle East investment; management targets 8-9% stable margin in 4-5 quarters, with recovery expected by Q2-Q3.

BFSI rotation rather than expansion, GST 2.0 driven client exits, and the paused power distribution rollout (about 1/4 of the INR25 crore smart meter target installed); monitor whether these stay episodic.
Labour code cost pass-through and Karnataka minimum wage matter in the High Court; management expects no direct margin impact but a possible slight PAPM uplift on variable markup contracts.
key_quotes: So the news is the consolidated revenue for the quarter was INR3,056 crores, which is up 6% year-on-year and 4% sequentially.
Ramani Dathi: Well, the effort is there. We may or may not be able to do it.
Ramani Dathi: This is the current run rate. So this run rate will continue for future quarters as well.

Balasubramanian A.: With respect to volume growth for numerous reasons that we called out earlier during our commentary, yes, it's become harder to forecast, but that's more of a demand side situation
summary.management_tone: Confident on portfolio mix, HR services (EdTech and RegTech) and specialised staffing, but cautious on general staffing volumes and FY27 EBITDA, where management declined to commit to the 20% growth target. Evasive on specific markup improvement and on the drivers of the unallocated cost increase, which were answered only at a high level.
